data.exact_reserve_text: During 2017, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2015 & prior) reduced by GBP 10.1m. This was mainly due to favourable claims experience in Director and Officers, Marine Liability and Marine Cargo resulting in reserve releases in line with standard actuarial techniques. This was offset by net ultimate claims increases in International Construction (adverse attritional and large loss development on Starr coverholder business), Professional Indemnity (large losses reported in the year; Appleby, Shepherd Building Group, Precision and Pitcher Partners) and General Liability (adverse attritional development).

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding stood at GBP 506.799m and at 31 December 2017 gross claims outstanding were GBP 480.244m. The report highlights a net reduction in prior underwriting years (2015 & prior) of GBP 10.1m driven by favourable claims experience in Director & Officers and Marine classes which produced reserve releases, partly offset by adverse development in International Construction, Professional Indemnity (several large reported losses) and General Liability which increased reserves. The closing position was also materially affected by foreign exchange movements noted in the technical provisions reconciliation.

data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year development (GROSS movement) not explicitly stated in the notes. The report provides a net prior-year reduction of GBP 10.1m (page 40). A gross reconciliation table is present (page 32) showing opening and closing gross claims outstanding and FX movements; closing < opening driven largely by foreign exchange effects. A gross claims development triangle is provided (pages 39-40) but the precise per-year diagonal comparisons were not fully extracted here, so no authoritative aggregated gross prior year development figure has been reported. Users should treat prior_year_development_gbp_m as unavailable (null) and rely on the net GBP 10.1m statement and the reconciliation/triangle for further analysis.
